interpretation: Business strength alone is a weak discriminator: 17/25 major winners and 14/25 major losers had strong or exceptional business DNA.
Inflection/expectations separate the groups more clearly in this first pass: 10/25 winners versus 4/25 losers were tagged strong or exceptional.
Losers carried more Anti-DNA flags on average (1.72 versus 1.24), but the gap is not large enough to rely on raw flag count alone.
The hardest cases are strong-business losers such as APP, PODD, CSGP, BSX, NFLX, HII, NRG and FICO. These require valuation, expectations, event/concentration risk and market-confirmation analysis.
Some major winners, including MRNA and INTC, were catalyst/turnaround cases and would be missed by a pure high-growth template. Monster archetype must be explicit.

Price momentum alone also needs a quality check: a strong pre-period price move can reflect genuine acceleration or late-cycle/exhaustion. Momentum should count only when aligned with improving business/expectations evidence.
v2RefinementsToTest: Replace generic Market Confirmation with Market Confirmation & Alignment.
Add an exhaustion penalty when price strength is extreme but business/expectations are deteriorating.
Increase importance of latest-quarter acceleration and guidance/expectation change relative to absolute historical growth.
Treat valuation as an expectations burden, not a standalone cheap/expensive score.
Use archetype-specific evidence for Operating Acceleration, Platform Reacceleration, Turnaround/Re-rating, Catalyst/Event and Cyclical Inflection cases.
Require a reason-for-move thesis that is supported by evidence available at the historical cutoff.
